target_customer: Bloggers, marketers and brands tracking conversations across blog comments and social media
problem: Blog comments were scattered across sites with no way to search or track them; BackType aggregated them and later offered social analytics.
business_model: Freemium search and analytics with an API; later aimed at brands
product_category: Social media and comment search and analytics

founders.name: Christopher Golda
founders.background_notes: YC page: after BackType launched Twitter Ads and ran Ads Center until 2014; now a YC General Partner

founders.name: Michael Montano
founders.background_notes: YC page: later Head of Engineering at Twitter and Partner at True Ventures

competitors.name: JS-Kit
competitors.what: Comment and widget service for blogs

technical_complexity.rationale: Crawled and scraped comments from millions of blogs, indexed them for search and matched commenters across sites; later built big data tooling (Cascalog, ElephantDB, Storm).

defensibility.rationale: Aggregated comment data had value but did not require site participation, which also made it easy for others to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Twitter acquired BackType in July 2011 and discontinued the product and API.

market_need_then: Blog commenting was a large conversation layer in 2008 and Twitter was rising; TechCrunch described BackType as Twitter for comments and found useful results for events such as TechCrunch50.

branding.brand_signature: Open source Storm and Cascalog from the BackType engineering team
branding.community_and_virality: Third party tools built on its API such as ConvoTrack; Storm was open sourced in September 2011 and became an Apache top level project in 2014

brand_strength.rationale: Known among bloggers and developers; the lasting brand impact was the Storm project, not the BackType name.

pivots.why: Broaden beyond blog comments; exact dates not confirmed

outcome_analysis: BackType launched in August 2008 as a search engine for blog comments, raised about 300,000 from True Ventures in March 2009, and widened to social analytics and big data tooling. Twitter acquired it in July 2011, discontinued the product and kept the team, and the Storm stream processor built there became an influential open source project; the price was not disclosed.
notes: The 300K figure comes from a PaidContent headline linked on the True Ventures post (the post itself does not state the amount). Seedtable and Wikipedia list 15K from YC (unverified aggregator figure, not recorded as a round). backtype.com returned HTTP 503. Founder education and prior employers not found. Name origin not found.
